sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page sapa1254 'Sapara' and subgroup page para1308 'Paravilhana-Pauxiana'
sources.note: Lists only d'Almada 1861 [1787], Koch-Grünberg 1928 and Girard 1971 (subclassification) for the language; the subgroup page cites Meira 2006, Howard 2001, Gildea 2012 for subclassification. No grammar, sketch or phonology exists for Sapará in Glottolog (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sapará language' (cites Migliazza 1985, Schomburgk 1848, Gildea 2003, Kaufman 2007, Farabee 1924)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress; reports Schomburgk's 1848 remark that Sapará was 'the Macusi idiom with very slight and dialectic variations'.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco. Ergebnisse einer Reise in Nordbrasilien und Venezuela in den Jahren 1911-1913. Vierter Band: Sprachen. Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder. Section 'Sapará, Purukotó, Wayumará', pp. 257-272; 'Zur Transskription', pp. 2-3.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary linguistic data on Sapará: a three-column comparative wordlist (Sapará / Purukotó / Wayumará) with acute accent marks on the forms (p. 258: onú 'Zunge', uyóe 'Zahn', uyonaí 'Nase', uyonayatáń 'Nasenloch', uyo:nú 'Auge', upa:naí 'Ohr', apepé, une:kapú 'Kopf', ipo:putú 'Kopfhaar', uyomekúń 'Arm'; p. 257 eleuta-ké 'setze dich!', iue:-ké 'töte!', mia:lé 'vorwärts!'), i.e. the accent mostly sits on the final syllable of citation forms; but no stress rule is stated anywhere. The general 'Zur Transskription' note (pp. 2-3) only says that i/u bearing an accent count as diphthong memb…

sources.citation: Farabee, William Curtis. 1924. The Central Caribs. University Museum Anthropological Publications 10. Philadelphia. 'Zaparas', pp. 242-243.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic note only: three full-bloods remained c. 1914, the mother 'speaks only her own language, which is very closely related to Macusi'; a vocabulary is given for Azumara but none for Zapara; nothing on accent.

sources.citation: d'Almada, Manuel da Gama Lobo. 1861 [1787]. Descripção relativa ao Rio Branco e seu território. Revista Trimensal do Instituto Historico, Geographico e Ethnographico do Brasil 24: 617-683.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only an ethnographic paragraph 'Saparás' (pp. 678-679: they live on the Mucajaí, deserted the Portuguese settlements, led the 1781 killings); no vocabulary and nothing about the language found in the scanned.
